## Property: `name`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Environment variable name exposed to the container (e.g., `DATABASE_PASSWORD`, `API_KEY`).

docs.title: SecretEnvironmentVar API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `valueFrom`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Secret source injected by the container runtime.

Use an exact `$SsmParam(...)` or `$Secret(...)` directive. Unlike `environment`, Stacktape passes only the
parameter or secret ARN to the container orchestrator; the sensitive value is never stored in the task
definition.

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content: # SecurityScanningConfig API Reference

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `enabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `true`

Turns security scanning on or off for this stack.

When enabled, every deployment evaluates the resolved configuration against Stacktape's security rules, records
which packages the source tree and the rebuilt container images use (a CycloneDX inventory stored in the stack's
deployment bucket), and reports the findings and the inventory's location to the Security section of the
Stacktape Console, which grades the packages against known vulnerabilities. Findings describe risky settings,
for example a database reachable from the internet or a secret stored as a plain environment variable. When
disabled, nothing is evaluated, recorded or uploaded for this stack.

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stages`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Limits security scanning to the listed stages.

When omitted or empty, every stage is scanned. Stage names are matched exactly.

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  securityScanning:
    stages: [production, staging]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content: # ServiceHelperContainer API Reference

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `containerType`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "always-running" | "run-on-init"`

When and how this sidecar container runs.

**`run-on-init`**: Must exit with code 0 before the main container starts. Use for migrations or setup.
**`always-running`**: Runs alongside the main container for its entire lifetime. If it crashes, the whole task fails.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      sideContainers:
        - name: migrations
          containerType: run-on-init
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `name`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Unique container name within this workload.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `packaging`

- Required: yes
- Type: `js-bundle | prebuilt-image | dockerfile | buildpack`

How to build or specify the container image.

Choices:
- `js-bundle` (`JsBundleCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a bundled JavaScript or TypeScript entry file.. Properties: `requiresGlibcBinaries?: boolean`, `customDockerBuildCommands?: Array<string>`, `runtime?: string: "bun" | "deno" | "node"`, `entryfilePath: string`, `includeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeDependencies?: Array<string>`, `tsConfigPath?: string`, `emitTsDecoratorMetadata?: boolean`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle?: Array<string>`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage?: Array<string>`, `outputModuleFormat?: string: "cjs" | "esm"`, `nodeVersion?: number: 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24`, `disableSourceMaps?: boolean`, `outputSourceMapsTo?: string`, `minify?: boolean`, `minifyIdentifiers?: boolean`, `bundleAwsSdk?: boolean`.
- `prebuilt-image` (`PrebuiltCwImagePackaging`) — Uses a pre-built container image.. Properties: `repositoryCredentialsSecretArn?: string`, `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `image: string`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `dockerfile` (`DockerfileCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from your own Dockerfile.. Properties: `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `dockerfilePath?: string`, `buildContextPath: string`, `buildArgs?: Array<DockerBuildArg>`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `buildpack` (`BuildpackCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a project directory without a Dockerfile.. Properties: `sourceDirectoryPath?: string`, `startCommand?: string`, `buildCommand?: string`, `installCommand?: string`, `packages?: unknown`, `aptPackages?: Array<string>`, `buildEnvironment?: Array<EnvironmentVar>`, `railpackConfig?: unknown`.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: dockerfile
            properties:
              buildContextPath: ./api
              dockerfilePath: Dockerfile
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `dependsOn`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ContainerDependency>`

Start this container only after the listed containers reach a specific state.

E.g., wait for a database sidecar to be `HEALTHY` before starting the app container.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: migrations
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
          essential: false
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          dependsOn:
            - containerName: migrations
              condition: SUCCESS
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment variables injected at runtime. Use `$ResourceParam()` or `$Secret()` for dynamic values.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          environment:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: production
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: $ResourceParam('appDb', 'connectionString')
            - name: STRIPE_KEY
              value: $Secret('stripe.secretKey')
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - appDb
  appDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db.password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `essential`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`

If `true` (default), the entire workload restarts when this container fails.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
        - name: metrics-sidecar
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: prom/statsd-exporter:latest
          essential: false
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `internalHealthCheck`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerHealthCheck`

Command-based health check. If it fails on an essential container, the workload instance is replaced.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          internalHealthCheck:
            healthCheckCommand:
              - CMD-SHELL
              - curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
            intervalSeconds: 30
            retries: 3
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logging`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadContainerLogging`

Container logging (stdout/stderr). Sent to CloudWatch, viewable with `stacktape logs`.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          logging:
            retentionDays: 14
            disabled: false
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `secrets`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<SecretEnvironmentVar>`

Sensitive environment variables fetched by ECS instead of stored in the task definition.

Each `valueFrom` must be an exact `$SsmParam(...)` or `$Secret(...)` directive.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stopTimeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `30`

Seconds to wait after SIGTERM before SIGKILL (2-120).

A full deploy waits until the old containers have stopped, so an app that ignores `SIGTERM` makes every deploy
up to this much slower. Exit once in-flight work is done. A hot-swap deploy lets old containers stop in the
background. Services with a gradual `deployment` (blue/green) default to 2 seconds.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          stopTimeout: 60
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

```yaml
resources:

    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          volumeMounts:
            - type: efs
              properties:
                efsFilesystemName: sharedStorage
                mountPath: /data

        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
  sharedStorage:
    type: efs-filesystem
```

StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `disableStackInfoSaving`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Stop saving stack info to a local file after each deployment.

By default, Stacktape saves resource details and custom outputs to
`.stacktape-stack-info/{stackName}.json` after every deploy.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  disableStackInfoSaving: true
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `nat`

- Required: no
- Type: `NatSettings | option-2`

NAT: outbound internet for workloads in the private subnets.

Who uses it:

container workloads with `usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true` (they cannot run without it, so setting that flag
requires `nat`);
Lambda functions with `joinDefaultVpc: true`, which have no internet access at all until `nat` is set;
AgentCore runtimes that connect to VPC-only resources.

Pick `ec2` (one small instance, ~$7/month, no failover), `ha-ec2` (one instance per availability zone with
automatic failover, ~$7/month per zone) or `gateway` (AWS-managed NAT Gateways, ~$32/month per zone plus
$0.045 per GB). Switching between kinds keeps the VPC and subnets, but the public IPs change.

With `vpc.reuseVpc`, the reused VPC's own NAT is used and this setting creates nothing; set it to any kind to
place this stack's VPC functions in the reused VPC's private subnets.

Choices:
- `NatSettings` (`NatSettings`). Properties: `type: string: "ec2" | "gateway" | "ha-ec2"`, `instanceSize?: string`, `availabilityZones?: number: 2 | 3`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat: ha-ec2
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `outputs`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<StackOutput>`

Custom values to display and save after each deployment.

Use outputs to surface dynamic values like API URLs, database endpoints, or resource ARNs
that are only known after deployment. Outputs are:

Printed in the terminal after deploy
Saved to the stack info JSON file
Optionally exported for cross-stack references (via `export: true`)

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  outputs:
    - name: ApiUrl
      value: $ResourceParam('api', 'url')
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

StackConfig API Reference

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `.stacktape-stack-info/`

Directory for the stack info JSON file.

Relative to the project root.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  stackInfoDirectory: ./build/stack-info
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stageType`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "non-production" | "production"`

Explicitly classifies this stack's stage as production or not.

The classification drives everything that treats production differently: error-tracking
incidents (every production error group enters the incident queue), the stricter
delete-production permission, deploy gates, AI remediation autonomy limits, and the severity
of security findings (a database reachable from the internet is `HIGH` in production and `LOW`
elsewhere; production-only findings such as missing deletion protection are listed by
`stacktape validate` but not reported for other stages).

When omitted, the type chosen when the stage was created in the Stacktape Console decides.
Without either, Stacktape infers it from the stage name: `prod`, `production`, `prd`, and `live`
(case-insensitive, including segmented variants like `prod-eu` or `client-a-prod` and numbered
ones like `prod2`) count as production, while names carrying a rehearsal marker (`pre-prod`,
`prod-test`, `staging-live`) do not. Set it explicitly when your naming does not follow those
conventions.

This is a per-stage classification: with a TypeScript config, branch on the `stage` argument
to return different values for different stages.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  stageType: production
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tags`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<CloudformationTag>`

Tags applied to every AWS resource in this stack.

Useful for cost tracking, access control, and organization. Stacktape automatically
adds `projectName`, `stage`, and `stackName` tags — your custom tags are merged on top.

Max 45 tags.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tags:
    - name: team
      value: payments
    - name: costCenter
      value: '4100'
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tracing`

- Required: no
- Type: `TracingOptions`

Stack-wide distributed tracing default.

Applies to every resource in the stack that supports tracing. Individual resources can override
it with their own `tracing` property (`false` opts a resource out). Enabling tracing requires no
code changes for Lambda-based resources — Stacktape attaches the OpenTelemetry instrumentation
automatically.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
```

StackConfig API Reference

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Resource`

- Required: yes
- Type: `Array<string>`

ARNs of the AWS resources this statement applies to. Use `"*"` for all resources.

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Resource:
            - '*'
          Action:
            - rekognition:DetectLabels
            - rekognition:DetectText
```

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Action`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

AWS actions to allow or deny (e.g., `s3:GetObject`, `sqs:SendMessage`).

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Condition`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Conditions under which this statement applies (e.g., IP restrictions, tag-based access).

**Example (YAML):**

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - s3:GetObject
          Resource:
            - 'arn:aws:s3:::my-secure-bucket/*'
          Condition:
            Bool:
              'aws:SecureTransport': 'true'
```

**Example (TypeScript):**

```ts
import { WebService, defineConfig, JsBundleImagePackaging } from 'stacktape';

export default defineConfig(() => {
  const api = new WebService({
    packaging: new JsBundleImagePackaging({ entryfilePath: 'src/server.ts' }),
    resources: { cpu: 0.25, memory: 512 },
    iamRoleStatements: [
      {
        Effect: 'Allow',
        Action: ['s3:GetObject'],
        Resource: ['arn:aws:s3:::my-secure-bucket/*'],
        Condition: { Bool: { 'aws:SecureTransport': 'true' } }
      }
    ]
  });

  return { resources: { api } };
});
```

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Effect`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `Allow`

Whether to allow or deny the specified actions.

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Sid`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Optional identifier for this statement (for readability).

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Sid: AllowBedrockInvoke
          Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - bedrock:InvokeModel
          Resource:
            - 'arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/*'
```

VpcSettings API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `reuseVpc`

- Required: no
- Type: `VpcReuseConfig`

Share a VPC with another Stacktape stack or use an existing VPC.

Useful when this stack needs to access VPC-protected resources (databases, Redis)
from another stack. By default, each stack gets its own VPC.

**Important:** Set this when first creating the stack. Adding it to an already
deployed stack can cause resources to be replaced and **data to be lost**.

docs.content:
# HostingBucket API Reference

Host a static website (React, Vue, Astro, etc.) on S3 + CloudFront CDN.

Resource type: `hosting-bucket`

docs.title: HostingBucket API Reference
HostingBucket API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `properties`

- Required: yes
- Type: `HostingBucketProps`

docs.title: HostingBucket API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: HostingBucket API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

Resource type: `hosting-bucket`

docs.title: HostingBucketBuild API Reference
HostingBucketBuild API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `command`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Command to run (e.g., `npm run build`, `vite build`, `npm run dev`).

Runs through the system shell, so `npm ci && npm run build` works as written. When `workingDirectory` has its own
`package.json`, Stacktape installs its dependencies first.

docs.title: HostingBucketBuild API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
        workingDirectory: .
```

HostingBucketBuild API Reference

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `.`

Working directory for the command (relative to project root).

docs.content:

```yaml
resources:
```

# HostingBucketProps API Reference

Resource type: `hosting-bucket`

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `uploadDirectoryPath`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Path to the build output directory (e.g., `dist`, `build`, `out`).

This folder's contents are uploaded to the bucket on every deploy.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app

        command: npm run build
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `build`

- Required: no
- Type: `HostingBucketBuild`

Build command that produces the files to upload (e.g., `npm run build`).

Runs during the packaging phase, in parallel with other resources. Bundle size is shown in deploy logs.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
```

HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `customDomains`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<DomainConfiguration>`

Custom domains (e.g., `www.example.com`). Stacktape auto-creates DNS records and TLS certificates.

Your domain must be added as a Route53 hosted zone in your AWS account first.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
```

HostingBucketProps API Reference

- Required: no
- Type: `HostingBucketBuild`

Dev server command for local development (e.g., `npm run dev`, `vite`).

Used by `stacktape dev`.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
```

HostingBucketProps API Reference

## Property: `disableUrlNormalization`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Disable clean URL normalization (e.g., `/about` → `/about.html`).

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
```

HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `edgeFunctions`

- Required: no
- Type: `EdgeFunctionsConfig`

Run edge functions on CDN requests/responses (URL rewrites, auth, A/B testing).

`onRequest`: Before cache lookup and before forwarding to the bucket.
`onResponse`: Before returning the response to the client.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  authChecker:
    type: edge-lambda-function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./edge/auth.ts
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
      edgeFunctions:
        onRequest: authChecker
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `errorDocument`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Page to show for 404 errors (e.g., `/error.html`).

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: static-website
      build:
        command: npm run build
      errorDocument: /error.html
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `excludeFilesPatterns`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Glob patterns for files to skip during upload (relative to `uploadDirectoryPath`).

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: static-website
      build:
        command: npm run build
      excludeFilesPatterns:
        - '**/*.map'
        - 'stats.html'
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `fileOptions`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<DirectoryUploadFilter>`

Set HTTP headers (e.g., `Cache-Control`) for files matching specific patterns.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
      fileOptions:
        - includePattern: 'assets/**'
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control
              value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `hostingContentType`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "astro-static-website" | "gatsby-static-website" | "nuxt-static-website" | "single-page-app" | "static-website" | "sveltekit-static-website"`
- Default: `static-website`

Optimizes caching and routing for your type of frontend app.

**`single-page-app`**: For React, Vue, Angular, or any SPA built with Vite/Webpack.
Enables client-side routing (e.g., `/about` serves `index.html`). HTML is never browser-cached;
hashed assets (`.js`, `.css`) are cached forever.

**`static-website`** (default): For multi-page static sites. All files are CDN-cached
but never browser-cached, so users always see the latest content after a deploy.

**`astro-static-website`** / **`sveltekit-static-website`** / **`nuxt-static-website`**:
Framework-specific presets that cache hashed build assets (`_astro/`, `_app/`, `_nuxt/`)
indefinitely while keeping HTML fresh.

**`gatsby-static-website`**: Gatsby-specific caching following their recommendations.

You can override any preset's behavior using `fileOptions`.

## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "infrequent-access" | "standard"`
- Default: `standard`

Choose the lower-ingestion-cost CloudWatch Logs class for logs that you inspect only occasionally.

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription
filters, embedded metrics, or Stacktape log forwarding. A log group's class cannot be changed after it is
created, so use this for new resources or stages.

docs.content:
## Property: `logForwarding`

- Required: no
- Type: `http-endpoint | highlight | datadog`

Forward logs to an external service (Datadog, Highlight.io, or any HTTP endpoint).

Uses Kinesis Data Firehose (~$0.03/GB). Failed deliveries go to a backup S3 bucket.

Choices:
- `http-endpoint` (`HttpEndpointLogForwarding`). Properties: `endpointUrl: string`, `gzipEncodingEnabled?: boolean`, `parameters?: unknown`, `retryDuration?: number`, `accessKey?: string`.
- `highlight` (`HighlightLogForwarding`). Properties: `projectId: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.
- `datadog` (`DatadogLogForwarding`). Properties: `apiKey: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

    properties:

      memory: 512
      timeout: 10
      logging:
        retentionDays: 90
        logForwarding:

```

docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: HttpApiGateway API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

# KinesisStreamProps API Reference

Resource type: `kinesis-stream`

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `capacityMode`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "ON_DEMAND" | "PROVISIONED"`
- Default: `ON_DEMAND`

How the stream scales.

**`ON_DEMAND`**: Auto-scales, pay per GB. Recommended for most use cases.
**`PROVISIONED`**: You choose a fixed number of shards (1 MB/s write, 2 MB/s read each). More predictable costs.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# capacityMode
resources:
  eventStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      retentionPeriodHours: 48
  streamProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-records.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: eventStream
            batchSize: 100
            startingPosition: LATEST
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `enableEnhancedFanOut`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Give each consumer its own dedicated 2 MB/s read throughput (instead of sharing).

Use when you have multiple consumers reading from the same stream and need low latency.
Enhanced fan-out consumers are auto-created when a Lambda uses `autoCreateConsumer: true`.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# enableEnhancedFanOut
resources:
  fanoutStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      enableEnhancedFanOut: true
  realtimeConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/realtime.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: fanoutStream
            autoCreateConsumer: true
            startingPosition: LATEST
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `encryption`

- Required: no
- Type: `KinesisStreamEncryption`

Encrypt data at rest using a KMS key.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# encryption
resources:
  secureStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      encryption:
        enabled: true

    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle

          properties:

```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `retentionPeriodHours`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `24`

How long records stay in the stream (hours). Range: 24–8,760 (365 days). Beyond 24h costs extra.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# retentionPeriodHours
resources:
  auditTrail:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      retentionPeriodHours: 168
  auditConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/audit.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: auditTrail
            startingPosition: TRIM_HORIZON
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `shardCount`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `1`

Number of shards. Only used when `capacityMode` is `PROVISIONED`.

Each shard: 1 MB/s write (1,000 records/s), 2 MB/s read (shared across consumers).

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# shardCount
resources:
  clickstream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: PROVISIONED
      shardCount: 4
      retentionPeriodHours: 72
  analyticsConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/analytics.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: clickstream
            batchSize: 500
```

docs.content:
## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "infrequent-access" | "standard"`
- Default: `standard`

Choose the lower-ingestion-cost CloudWatch Logs class for logs that you inspect only occasionally.

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription
filters, embedded metrics, or Stacktape log forwarding. A log group's class cannot be changed after it is
created, so use this for new resources or stages.

```yaml
    type: function
    properties:

        logClass: infrequent-access
```

docs.title: LogForwardingBase API Reference

docs.content:
## Property: `logForwarding`

- Required: no
- Type: `http-endpoint | highlight | datadog`

Forward logs to an external service (Datadog, Highlight.io, or any HTTP endpoint).

Uses Kinesis Data Firehose (~$0.03/GB). Failed deliveries go to a backup S3 bucket.

Choices:
- `http-endpoint` (`HttpEndpointLogForwarding`). Properties: `endpointUrl: string`, `gzipEncodingEnabled?: boolean`, `parameters?: unknown`, `retryDuration?: number`, `accessKey?: string`.
- `highlight` (`HighlightLogForwarding`). Properties: `projectId: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.
- `datadog` (`DatadogLogForwarding`). Properties: `apiKey: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.

# MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference

Resource type: `mongo-db-atlas-cluster`

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `accessibilityMode`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "internet" | "scoping-workloads-in-vpc" | "vpc" | "whitelisted-ips-only"`
- Default: `internet`

Network access mode.

**`internet`**: Accessible from anywhere (credentials still required).
**`vpc`**: Only from resources in your VPC + any `whitelistedIps`.
**`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`**: Like `vpc`, but also requires security-group access via `connectTo`.
**`whitelisted-ips-only`**: Only from IP addresses listed in `whitelistedIps`.

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
providerConfig:
  mongoDbAtlas:
    organizationId: 5f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e
    publicKey: abcdefgh
    privateKey: $Secret('mongo-atlas-private-key')
    accessibility:
      accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
resources:
  appDb:
    type: mongo-db-atlas-cluster
    properties:
      clusterTier: M10
      version: '7.0'
      enableBackups: true
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      connectTo:
        - appDb
```

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `whitelistedIps`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to access the cluster (e.g., your office IP).

No effect in `internet` mode. In `vpc`/`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`, adds access for IPs outside the VPC.
In `whitelisted-ips-only`, these are the only IPs that can connect.

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
providerConfig:

    organizationId: 5f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e
    publicKey: abcdefgh
    privateKey: $Secret('mongo-atlas-private-key')
    accessibility:
      accessibilityMode: whitelisted-ips-only
      whitelistedIps:
        - 203.0.113.10
        - 198.51.100.0/24
resources:
  appDb:
    type: mongo-db-atlas-cluster
    properties:
      clusterTier: M10
      version: '7.0'
      enableBackups: true
```

# ContainerDependency API Reference

Resource type: `multi-container-workload`

docs.title: ContainerDependency API Reference
ContainerDependency API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `condition`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "COMPLETE" | "HEALTHY" | "START" | "SUCCESS"`

The condition that the dependency container must meet.

Available conditions:

`START`: The dependency has started.
`COMPLETE`: The dependency has finished executing (regardless of success).
`SUCCESS`: The dependency has finished with an exit code of `0`.
`HEALTHY`: The dependency has passed its first health check.

docs.title: ContainerDependency API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: redis
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: redis:7
          internalHealthCheck:
            healthCheckCommand:
              - CMD-SHELL
              - redis-cli ping || exit 1
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          dependsOn:
            - containerName: redis
              condition: HEALTHY
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

```yaml
      engine:

        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro

```

docs.content:
## Property: `packaging`

- Required: yes
- Type: `js-bundle | prebuilt-image | dockerfile | buildpack`

How to build or specify the container image.

Choices:
- `js-bundle` (`JsBundleCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a bundled JavaScript or TypeScript entry file.. Properties: `requiresGlibcBinaries?: boolean`, `customDockerBuildCommands?: Array<string>`, `runtime?: string: "bun" | "deno" | "node"`, `entryfilePath: string`, `includeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeDependencies?: Array<string>`, `tsConfigPath?: string`, `emitTsDecoratorMetadata?: boolean`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle?: Array<string>`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage?: Array<string>`, `outputModuleFormat?: string: "cjs" | "esm"`, `nodeVersion?: number: 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24`, `disableSourceMaps?: boolean`, `outputSourceMapsTo?: string`, `minify?: boolean`, `minifyIdentifiers?: boolean`, `bundleAwsSdk?: boolean`.
- `prebuilt-image` (`PrebuiltCwImagePackaging`) — Uses a pre-built container image.. Properties: `repositoryCredentialsSecretArn?: string`, `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `image: string`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `dockerfile` (`DockerfileCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from your own Dockerfile.. Properties: `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `dockerfilePath?: string`, `buildContextPath: string`, `buildArgs?: Array<DockerBuildArg>`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `buildpack` (`BuildpackCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a project directory without a Dockerfile.. Properties: `sourceDirectoryPath?: string`, `startCommand?: string`, `buildCommand?: string`, `installCommand?: string`, `packages?: unknown`, `aptPackages?: Array<string>`, `buildEnvironment?: Array<EnvironmentVar>`, `railpackConfig?: unknown`.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)


ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `events`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<application-load-balancer | http-api-gateway | workload-internal | service-connect | network-load-balancer>`

How this container receives traffic (API Gateway, load balancer, or service-connect).

Choices:
- `application-load-balancer` (`ContainerWorkloadLoadBalancerIntegration`) — Triggers a container when a request matches the specified conditions on an Application Load Balancer.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `loadBalancerName: string`, `listenerPort?: number`, `priority: number`, `paths?: Array<string>`, `methods?: Array<string>`, `hosts?: Array<string>`, `headers?: Array<LbHeaderCondition>`, `queryParams?: Array<LbQueryParamCondition>`, `sourceIps?: Array<string>`.
- `http-api-gateway` (`ContainerWorkloadHttpApiIntegration`) — Triggers a container when an HTTP API Gateway receives a matching request.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `httpApiGatewayName: string`, `method: string: "*" | "DELETE" | "GET" | "HEAD" | "OPTIONS" | "PATCH" | "POST" | "PUT"`, `path: string`, `authorizer?: cognito | lambda | aws-iam`, `payloadFormat?: string: "1.0" | "2.0"`.
- `workload-internal` (`ContainerWorkloadInternalIntegration`) — Opens a container port for connections from other containers within the same workload.. Properties: `containerPort: number`.
- `service-connect` (`ContainerWorkloadServiceConnectIntegration`) — Opens a container port for connections from other compute resources in the same stack.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `alias?: string`, `protocol?: string: "grpc" | "http" | "http2"`.
- `network-load-balancer` (`ContainerWorkloadNetworkLoadBalancerIntegration`) — Triggers a container when a request is made to a Network Load Balancer.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `loadBalancerName: string`, `listenerPort: number`.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: web
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/index.ts
          events:
            - type: application-load-balancer
              properties:
                loadBalancerName: appLb
                priority: 1
                paths:
                  - /*
                containerPort: 3000
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
  appLb:
    type: application-load-balancer
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stopTimeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `30`

Seconds to wait after SIGTERM before SIGKILL (2-120).

A full deploy waits until the old containers have stopped, so an app that ignores `SIGTERM` makes every deploy
up to this much slower. Exit once in-flight work is done. A hot-swap deploy lets old containers stop in the
background. Services with a gradual `deployment` (blue/green) default to 2 seconds.

```yaml
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription

Resource type: `multi-container-workload`

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadDeploymentConfig API Reference
ContainerWorkloadDeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `strategy`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "AllAtOnce" | "Canary10Percent15Minutes" | "Canary10Percent5Minutes" | "Linear10PercentEvery1Minutes" | "Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes"`

How traffic shifts to the new version during deployment.

`Canary10Percent5Minutes`: 10% first, then all after 5 min.
`Canary10Percent15Minutes`: 10% first, then all after 15 min.
`Linear10PercentEvery1Minutes`: 10% more every minute.
`Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes`: 10% more every 3 minutes.
`AllAtOnce`: Instant switch.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadDeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: web
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/index.ts
          events:
            - type: application-load-balancer
              properties:
                loadBalancerName: appLb
                priority: 1
                containerPort: 3000
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      deployment:
        strategy: Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes
  appLb:
    type: application-load-balancer
  smokeTest:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/smoke-test.ts
```

## Property: `resources`

- Required: yes
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadResourcesConfig`

CPU, memory, and compute engine (Fargate or EC2).

**Fargate** (set `cpu` + `memory`): Serverless, no servers to manage.
**EC2** (set `instanceTypes`): Choose specific instance types for more control or GPU access.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

## Property: `tracing`

- Type: `TracingOptions | option-2`

Distributed tracing for this workload.

Overrides the stack-wide `stackConfig.tracing` setting: `false` opts this workload out, `true`
opts it in with the stack-wide sampling, an object opts it in with its own settings.

When enabled, Stacktape runs an OpenTelemetry collector as an additional container in the task
and points every container's OpenTelemetry SDK at it (`http://localhost:4318`) through standard
`OTEL_*` environment variables. The containers need the OpenTelemetry SDK in the application (any
language) — spans they emit are picked up without further configuration.

Traces are stored in your AWS account via X-Ray Transaction Search; see `stackConfig.tracing`
for the account-level effects.

Choices:
- `TracingOptions` (`TracingOptions`). Properties: `enabled?: boolean`, `samplingRate?: number`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  workers:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      tracing: true
      containers:
        - name: worker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Run the workload in the private subnets, without a public IP, with outbound traffic through the stack's NAT.

What you get: the container has no public IP, and all of its outbound internet traffic leaves through the stack's
NAT with one static Elastic IP per availability zone (useful when a third party allowlists your IPs).

Requires `stackConfig.nat` (`ec2`, `ha-ec2` or `gateway`); the cost depends on that choice, and `gateway` adds a
per-GB processing fee on top. Workloads that only talk to AWS services and other stack resources do not need it.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat: ha-ec2
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: worker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

EC2 instance types for the workload (e.g., `t3.medium`, `c6g.large`). Use instead of `cpu`/`memory`.

First type in the list is preferred. Instances auto-scale and are refreshed weekly for patching.
Tip: specify a single type and omit `cpu`/`memory` for optimal sizing.

docs.content:
## Property: `memory`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Memory in MB. Must be compatible with the vCPU count on Fargate.

Fargate valid combos: 0.25 vCPU → 512-2048 MB, 0.5 → 1024-4096, 1 → 2048-8192, 2 → 4096-16384,
4 → 8192-30720, 8 → 16384-61440, 16 → 32768-122880.
For EC2: auto-detected from instance type if omitted.

# NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference

TCP/TLS load balancer for non-HTTP traffic (MQTT, game servers, custom protocols).

Resource type: `network-load-balancer`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `properties`

- Required: yes
- Type: `NetworkLoadBalancerProps`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

```yaml
            type: js-bundle
```

## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

docs.content:
## Property: `channelName`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Name of a notification channel configured in the Stacktape Console.

Channels are created once per organization in the Console (**Monitoring** → **Channels**) and hold the
delivery credentials (Slack tokens, webhook URLs, ...). Referencing a channel by name lets many alarms and
uptime checks share one destination without repeating credentials in the config.

The referenced channel must exist in your organization — the deployment fails with a clear error if it
doesn't. Delivery happens through the Stacktape Console, so events routed to a console channel always
appear in the alert history.

docs.title: ConsoleChannelIntegrationProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiHealth:
    type: uptime-check
    properties:
      url: https://api.example.com/health
      notificationChannels:
        - type: console-channel
          properties:
            channelName: engineering-slack
```

docs.content:
## Property: `accessibilityMode`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "internet" | "scoping-workloads-in-vpc" | "vpc"`
- Default: `internet`

How the domain can be reached.

**`internet`**: Accessible from anywhere (still requires IAM credentials).
**`vpc`**: Only accessible from resources inside your VPC (functions with `joinDefaultVpc: true`, containers, batch jobs).
**`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`**: Like `vpc`, but also requires security-group access via `connectTo`.

**Cannot be changed after creation** — switching between internet and VPC modes requires a new domain.

docs.title: OpenSearchAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 2
      storage:
        size: 50
      accessibility:
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
  indexer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/indexer.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      connectTo:
        - searchEngine
```

- Required: yes

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Instance type for dedicated master nodes (e.g., `m5.large.search`). Manages cluster state, not data.

Recommended for clusters with 3+ data nodes to prevent split-brain. Use an odd count (3, 5, or 7).

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:

```yaml
  searchEngine:
```

OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `multiAzDisabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Disable Multi-AZ replication. Not recommended — reduces availability and data durability.

Multi-AZ is auto-enabled for clusters with 2+ nodes. It distributes nodes across availability zones
so the cluster survives an AZ outage.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: t3.medium.search
        instanceCount: 2
        multiAzDisabled: true
      storage:
        size: 20
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `standbyEnabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Enable Multi-AZ with a standby AZ for highest availability (99.99% SLA).

Distributes nodes across 3 AZs with one as standby. The standby takes over instantly during failures
without re-balancing. Requires: version 1.3+, 3 dedicated master + data nodes, GP3/SSD instances.

```yaml
        instanceCount: 3
        dedicatedMasterType: m5.large.search
        dedicatedMasterCount: 3

      storage:
        size: 50
```

- Required: no

Network access mode: public internet (default), VPC-only, or VPC with security-group scoping.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `packaging`

- Required: yes
- Type: `js-bundle | prebuilt-image | dockerfile | buildpack`

Configures the container image for the service.

Choices:
- `js-bundle` (`JsBundleCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a bundled JavaScript or TypeScript entry file.. Properties: `requiresGlibcBinaries?: boolean`, `customDockerBuildCommands?: Array<string>`, `runtime?: string: "bun" | "deno" | "node"`, `entryfilePath: string`, `includeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeDependencies?: Array<string>`, `tsConfigPath?: string`, `emitTsDecoratorMetadata?: boolean`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle?: Array<string>`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage?: Array<string>`, `outputModuleFormat?: string: "cjs" | "esm"`, `nodeVersion?: number: 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24`, `disableSourceMaps?: boolean`, `outputSourceMapsTo?: string`, `minify?: boolean`, `minifyIdentifiers?: boolean`, `bundleAwsSdk?: boolean`.
- `prebuilt-image` (`PrebuiltCwImagePackaging`) — Uses a pre-built container image.. Properties: `repositoryCredentialsSecretArn?: string`, `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `image: string`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `dockerfile` (`DockerfileCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from your own Dockerfile.. Properties: `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `dockerfilePath?: string`, `buildContextPath: string`, `buildArgs?: Array<DockerBuildArg>`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `buildpack` (`BuildpackCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a project directory without a Dockerfile.. Properties: `sourceDirectoryPath?: string`, `startCommand?: string`, `buildCommand?: string`, `installCommand?: string`, `packages?: unknown`, `aptPackages?: Array<string>`, `buildEnvironment?: Array<EnvironmentVar>`, `railpackConfig?: unknown`.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `resources`

- Required: yes
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadResourcesConfig`

CPU, memory, and compute engine for the container.

Two compute engines:

**Fargate** (default): Serverless — just specify `cpu` and `memory`.
**EC2**: Specify `instanceTypes` for more control and potentially lower cost.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:

    type: web-service

        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
        architecture: arm64
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment variables injected into the container at runtime.

Use for configuration like API keys, feature flags, or secrets.
Variables from `connectTo` (e.g., `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`) are added automatically.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      environment:
        - name: LOG_LEVEL
          value: info
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('mainDb', 'connectionString')
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.2'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference

```yaml
resources:
```

PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `sideContainers`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ServiceHelperContainer>`

Helper containers that run alongside the main container.

**`run-on-init`**: Runs to completion before the main container starts (e.g., database migrations).
**`always-running`**: Runs for the entire lifecycle (e.g., log forwarders, monitoring agents).
Can reach the main container via `localhost`.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stopTimeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `30`

Seconds to wait for graceful shutdown before force-killing the container.

The container receives `SIGTERM` first, then `SIGKILL` after this timeout. Must be 2-120.

A full deploy waits until the old containers have stopped, so an app that ignores `SIGTERM` makes every deploy
up to this much slower. Exit once in-flight work is done. A hot-swap deploy lets old containers stop in the
background. Services with a gradual `deployment` (blue/green) default to 2 seconds.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      stopTimeout: 60
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tracing`

- Required: no
- Type: `TracingOptions | option-2`

Distributed tracing for this service.

Overrides the stack-wide `stackConfig.tracing` setting: `false` opts this service out, `true`
opts it in with the stack-wide sampling, an object opts it in with its own settings.

When enabled, Stacktape runs an OpenTelemetry collector as a sidecar container and points the
service's OpenTelemetry SDK at it (`http://localhost:4318`) through standard `OTEL_*`
environment variables. The service needs the OpenTelemetry SDK in the application (any
language) — spans it emits are picked up without further configuration.

Traces are stored in your AWS account via X-Ray Transaction Search; see `stackConfig.tracing`
for the account-level effects.

Choices:
- `TracingOptions` (`TracingOptions`). Properties: `enabled?: boolean`, `samplingRate?: number`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      tracing:
        samplingRate: 0.5
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Run the workload in the private subnets, without a public IP, with outbound traffic through the stack's NAT.

What you get: the container has no public IP, and all of its outbound internet traffic leaves through the stack's
NAT with one static Elastic IP per availability zone (useful when a third party allowlists your IPs).

Requires `stackConfig.nat` (`ec2`, `ha-ec2` or `gateway`); the cost depends on that choice, and `gateway` adds a
per-GB processing fee on top. Workloads that only talk to AWS services and other stack resources do not need it.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat: ha-ec2
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `volumeMounts`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ContainerEfsMount>`

Persistent EFS volumes shared across containers and restarts.

Data stored in EFS volumes persists even when containers are replaced.
Multiple containers can mount the same volume. All data is encrypted in transit.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      volumeMounts:
        - type: efs
          properties:
            efsFilesystemName: sharedData
            mountPath: /data
  sharedData:
    type: efs-filesystem
    properties: {}
```

# Redis API Reference

Managed Redis-compatible in-memory store (Amazon ElastiCache) for caching, sessions, queues, and real-time data.

Resource type: `redis`

docs.title: Redis API Reference
Redis API Reference

- Required: yes

docs.title: Redis API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: Redis API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16.6'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

# RedisAccessibility API Reference

Resource type: `redis`

docs.title: RedisAccessibility API Reference
RedisAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `accessibilityMode`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "scoping-workloads-in-vpc" | "vpc"`
- Default: `vpc`

Who can connect to this cache.

**`vpc`** (default): Any resource in the same VPC (functions with `joinDefaultVpc: true`, containers, batch jobs).
**`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`**: Only resources that list this cache in their `connectTo`.

Caches don't have public IPs — you can't connect from your local machine directly.
Use a bastion host for local access.

Resource type: `redis`

## Property: `disabled`

- Required: no

Disable slow query logging.

- Required: no

Log format.

docs.title: RedisLogging API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "infrequent-access" | "standard"`
- Default: `standard`

Choose the lower-ingestion-cost CloudWatch Logs class for logs that you inspect only occasionally.

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription
filters, embedded metrics, or Stacktape log forwarding. A log group's class cannot be changed after it is
created, so use this for new resources or stages.

docs.content:

```yaml
resources:
  archiveWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/archive.ts
      logging:
        logClass: infrequent-access
```

Choices:

- `highlight` (`HighlightLogForwarding`). Properties: `projectId: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.
- `datadog` (`DatadogLogForwarding`). Properties: `apiKey: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.

RedisOssEngineProperties API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `instanceSize`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "cache.m4.10xlarge" | "cache.m4.2xlarge" | "cache.m4.4xlarge" | "cache.m4.large" | "cache.m4.xlarge" | "cache.m5.12xlarge" | "cache.m5.24xlarge" | "cache.m5.2xlarge" | "cache.m5.4xlarge" | "cache.m5.large" | "cache.m5.xlarge" | "cache.m6g.12xlarge" | "cache.m6g.16xlarge" | "cache.m6g.2xlarge" | "cache.m6g.4xlarge" | "cache.m6g.8xlarge" | "cache.m6g.large" | "cache.m6g.xlarge" | "cache.m7g.12xlarge" | "cache.m7g.16xlarge" | "cache.m7g.2xlarge" | "cache.m7g.4xlarge" | "cache.m7g.8xlarge" | "cache.m7g.large" | "cache.m7g.xlarge" | "cache.r4.16xlarge" | "cache.r4.2xlarge" | "cache.r4.4xlarge" | "cache.r4.8xlarge" | "cache.r4.large" | "cache.r4.xlarge" | "cache.r5.12xlarge" | "cache.r5.24xlarge" | "cache.r5.2xlarge" | "cache.r5.4xlarge" | "cache.r5.large" | "cache.r5.xlarge" | "cache.r6g.12xlarge" | "cache.r6g.16xlarge" | "cache.r6g.2xlarge" | "cache.r6g.4xlarge" | "cache.r6g.8xlarge" | "cache.r6g.large" | "cache.r6g.xlarge" | "cache.r7g.12xlarge" | "cache.r7g.16xlarge" | "cache.r7g.2xlarge" | "cache.r7g.4xlarge" | "cache.r7g.8xlarge" | "cache.r7g.large" | "cache.r7g.xlarge" | "cache.t2.medium" | "cache.t2.micro" | "cache.t2.small" | "cache.t3.medium" | "cache.t3.micro" | "cache.t3.small" | "cache.t4g.medium" | "cache.t4g.micro" | "cache.t4g.small"`

The size of each node. Affects memory, performance, and cost.

**Quick guide** (Valkey prices, Redis OSS is about 25% more):

**`cache.t4g.micro`** (~$0.013/hr, 0.5 GB): Development, testing, low-traffic apps.
**`cache.t4g.small`** (~$0.026/hr, 1.37 GB): Small production apps, session stores.
**`cache.m7g.large`** (~$0.12/hr, 6.38 GB): Production workloads with moderate data.
**`cache.r7g.large`** (~$0.16/hr, 13.07 GB): Large datasets, memory-heavy caching.

**Families:** `t` = burstable (cheap, variable). `m` = general purpose. `r` = memory-optimized.
Suffix `g` = ARM/Graviton (better price-performance).

This size applies to every node (primary + replicas). You can change it later without data loss.

```yaml
    type: redis

          instanceSize: cache.t4g.micro
```

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`

Auto-promote a replica to primary if the primary node fails.

Requires `numReplicaNodes >= 1`. Always enabled for sharded clusters.

Deploy replicas first, then enable failover in a separate deployment.
